A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PF-PPO work. The text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite changes to the title, authorship, structure, and layout.

before.justification: v2 reports original coding evaluations, reward-model and training analyses, and math-reasoning experiments in Appendix B, Table 5.

after.justification: v3 retains the original coding and math experiments and adds an eight-task evaluation in Section 5.6, Table 5.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same rank-based filtration, BoN/BR/BW weights, R2-based strategy selection, training objective, and Algorithm 2. Wording and notation corrections do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Section 5.6 adds a multitask study covering logic reasoning, math, code, STEM, complex tasks, instruction following, knowledge QA, and language understanding. This substantially extends evaluated coverage beyond the retained coding and math benchmarks. Ape210K and CMATH already appeared in v2 Appendix B.

E2.justification: The coding baselines and alternative filtering comparators are retained, including the merely abbreviated PPO-top-random and PPO-top-bottom. Math comparisons retain PPO-S under ORM, Oracle, and CRM rewards. The new multitask study also uses the existing PPO-S comparator.

E3.justification: The new study introduces a distinct evaluation design: one multitask model using the Doubao-25k policy/reward backbone, BO1 and BO5 accuracy, task-specific verifiers, and evaluation sets ranging from 680 to 4,466 cases. Existing coding settings remain unchanged; newly specified math-data details do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The filtering ablations, training curves, reward-reliability analyses, computational-cost comparison, and qualitative code examples are retained. Computational analysis moves to v3 Appendix C, while v2's qualitative Appendix C becomes Appendix B. The new multitask benchmarks do not introduce a separate ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: v3 Section 5.6 newly labels changes exceeding ±0.5% as statistically significant based on test-case counts, with corresponding highlighting in Table 5. No statistical test, confidence interval, or additional run count is specified. The ten repetitions used for reward-reliability plots are unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 5 adds results across eight tasks, including logic-reasoning BO1/BO5 accuracies of 48.9%/63.8% with reported PPO-S improvements of 2.3/2.8 points. Code and STEM have small negative BO1 deltas. All matched coding, math, filtering, computational, and qualitative results remain unchanged; the added scores concern new experimental conditions.

T1.justification: The MDP formulation, Bradley–Terry model, optimization objectives, filtration definitions, and R2 calculation are mathematically unchanged. Displaying the existing weight vectors as numbered Equation 5 adds no new theory, assumptions, or proof.

C1.justification: The title and main effectiveness claims broaden from a code-generation emphasis to reward-noise mitigation across reasoning tasks. The abstract explicitly includes math reasoning, and the conclusion removes its code-task restriction. The central PF-PPO contribution and stated coding performance margins remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 5.6 newly interprets the multitask results as demonstrating consistent effectiveness across diverse tasks. Existing explanations of reward noise, filtering benefits, Oracle performance, and R2's imperfect predictive value remain unchanged. No substantive new limitations analysis accompanies the broader interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 adds a specific code-repository link where v2 only refers to supplementary code. It also explicitly documents the retained math study's 200k Ape210K training split, 5k evaluation split, CMATH size, and answer-checking scripts. These are additional disclosures rather than demonstrated changes to existing experiments.

R1.justification: The cited works and Section 2's positioning relative to reward-model improvement, rejection sampling, supervised distillation, and constrained RLHF are retained. Bibliographic and citation-format changes do not add research positioning.

P1.justification: The experimental narrative is substantially reorganized: benchmark and dataset descriptions merge, baselines and coding results combine, training curves move, math experiments enter the main text, and computational analysis moves to an appendix. The title, abstract, introduction, author information, and concluding material are also revised.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column layout, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Figure 1 moves to the opening page, math and computational tables change locations, and a new multitask table is added. All four figures retain identical underlying plot images.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves documentation through explicit math-data and evaluation details and a code-access link, while preserving the existing evidence. Table 5 adds useful evidence about broader applicability. These gains are limited by sparse documentation of the new datasets, training, and verifiers, and an unexplained significance threshold. Its negligible code/STEM changes also qualify the claim of consistent effectiveness, so the revision does not establish a substantial overall improvement.
